gap: No result ChatGPT got states the maker's own rule for turning a label mAh into deliverable capacity. Anker's support FAQ says that rule is cell mAh × 3.7 V ÷ 5 V × 82% boost efficiency. Applied to the picks, a 20,000 mAh bank delivers about 60.7 Wh and the 24,000 mAh Anker 737 about 72.8 Wh. Against a 50 Wh Steam Deck OLED that is about 1.2 and 1.46 full charges before the Deck's own charging losses.
standout_why: I compared the rival pages ChatGPT cited: gamingonbatteries.com/best-power-bank-steam-deck, rallynomics.com and vgkami.com. I also checked the top result, itechguides.com. Gamingonbatteries already explains cell-voltage Wh at 3.7 V and assumes a 12% conversion loss. Rallynomics uses 3.6 V and 75% delivery. Vgkami quotes Anker's estimate of 63–70 Wh usable for the 25K. Itechguides has the point that total wattage is not per-port wattage. So the cell-versus-delivered idea is already covered. What none of them gives is each candidate's own printed rated capacity at 5 V or its Wh. Store rate limits stopped me getting those, so the angle only partly stands out.
decides: It confirms the pick and doesn't change it. Using the maker's own 82% figure, every 20,000 mAh candidate (INIU P62-E1, UGREEN 20K, Baseus Blade H1) works out to about 1.2 OLED charges, and the 24–25K banks to about 1.45–1.5. That matches the 'about 1.2 / about 1.5' column already on our page. Capacity therefore doesn't separate same-size banks, and price, weight and built-in cables decide the pick. One price note: the UGREEN 25K 165W with built-in cables that ChatGPT showed at $74.99 is $109.99 on us.ugreen.com today, so ChatGPT's 'best value' framing for it is out of date.

findings.label: Maker's method for rated (deliverable) capacity
findings.value: Cell mAh × 3.7 V ÷ 5 V × 0.82. Example: 10,000 mAh → 37 Wh → 7,400 mAh at 5 V → 6,068 mAh rated
findings.source_title: Why Is the Rated Capacity Marked on a Power Bank Lower Than Expected? (Anker Support)
findings.note: Anker states the cells run at 'around 3.7V', the rating is 'calculated at a standard output voltage of 5V', and the boost circuit has 'typically around 82% efficiency'. Applied to the candidates: 20,000 mAh → 74 Wh × 0.82 = 60.7 Wh; 24,000 mAh → 88.8 × 0.82 = 72.8 Wh; 25,000 mAh → 92.5 × 0.82 = 75.9 Wh. Some 25K banks are labelled 90 Wh, which implies 3.6 V cells and gives 73.8 Wh.

findings.label: Steam Deck OLED charges from each capacity class (maker's 82% rule)
findings.source_title: Best Power Banks for ROG Xbox Ally X and Steam Deck 2026 (Rallynomics)
findings.note: The Deck battery sizes (OLED 50 Wh, LCD 40 Wh) come from this page. I did not open Valve's own spec page. Arithmetic: 60.7/50 = 1.21; 72.8/50 = 1.46; 75.9/50 = 1.52. The Deck's own charging losses are not included. For LCD (40 Wh): 1.5 / 1.8 / 1.9.
